description: Documentation + final integration polish. Document the /admin editor: the auth mechanism (logged-in Sanity user, no master token), the required manual Sanity dashboard steps (CORS credentialed-write origins, inviting users with Editor/Admin roles, env vars), the daily authoring workflow, and how it coexists with /studio. Update env example if any new NEXT_PUBLIC_ var is used, and verify /studio and public rendering remain untouched. Depends on FEAT-001..003.
steps: Add a 'Custom Admin Editor (/admin)' section to README.md alongside the existing Sanity Studio section. Explain: it is an ADDITIVE WordPress-style editor at /admin (Studio at /studio still works); login uses each writer's own Sanity account (multi-user, roles managed in manage.sanity.io); the easy spreadsheet-style table creator solves the Studio table pain; content is saved back into the SAME Sanity dataset and is fully interchangeable with Studio.

Document the exact REQUIRED manual user steps: (1) In manage.sanity.io > API > CORS Origins, ensure http://localhost:3000, the Vercel URL, and https://coinscribed.com each have 'Allow credentials' CHECKED (needed for credentialed browser writes/uploads, not just reads). (2) Invite writers via Members > Invite with Editor role (and Administrator for owners); per-user roles + audit trail apply because writes run as the logged-in user. (3) Confirm NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET are set locally and on Vercel. Explicitly state that NO master/server write token is used or should be added.

Document the daily workflow: go to /admin, sign in with Sanity, see the article list, click New Article or Edit, fill fields, build the body with the rich-text toolbar, insert a table with the spreadsheet editor, upload images, then Save Draft or Publish. Note that Published articles appear on the public site within the existing cache window, same as Studio.

If FEAT-001..003 introduced any new NEXT_PUBLIC_ env var (e.g. an explicit app origin/base URL) or any dependency, update .env.example and note it in README; if none, state that no new env vars are required. Do NOT add any secret token to .env.example.

Final coexistence check: confirm app/studio/* , sanity.config.ts, sanity/schemas/*, lib/sanity.ts (read client), lib/sanity-queries.ts, and components/news/PortableTextRenderer.tsx are unchanged by this task (git diff), so the public site and Studio behavior are unaffected. If any were changed, justify or revert.
acceptance_criteria: README.md documents the /admin editor: additive to /studio, Sanity multi-user auth with roles, easy table creator, save-back to the same dataset.
README clearly lists the manual steps: CORS 'Allow credentials' for the app origins, inviting users with Editor/Admin roles, and the NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars; and states no master write token is used.
Daily authoring workflow is documented end to end including the table editor.
.env.example reflects reality (updated if a new NEXT_PUBLIC_ var was added; otherwise unchanged) and contains no secret token.
git diff confirms /studio, sanity.config.ts, sanity/schemas/*, lib/sanity.ts, lib/sanity-queries.ts, and components/news/PortableTextRenderer.tsx are unchanged (or changes are justified).
verification: Read README.md and .env.example to confirm the documented steps and env accuracy.
git diff --name-only against the branch base and confirm no unintended changes to /studio, schemas, read client, queries, or the public Portable Text renderer.
Rely on GitHub Actions CI for the final next build + next lint pass.
